caption: The drawing depicts a round, shallow dish or plate with an ornate design. The background color of the plate is a pale yellowish-cream with a brownish-red rim accented by a wavy, yellow internal border just inside the edge. In the center of the plate, there is a stylized bird with a pale yellow body, brown wings and tail, red and green markings on its feathers, a red beak, and a red spot near its eye. The bird is perched on a green leafy branch with two red flowers, which extends upward from a decorative banner toward the bottom of the plate that reads "A.H. 1808" in dark letters. On either side of the central tree are additional leafy green branches, each terminating in a stylized flower with green petals, white highlights, and a red circular center marked with a cross. Above the bird, two large, stylized, tulip-like flowers with green petals, red centers, and brown outlines curve inward from the left and right sides. The overall composition is symmetrical around the vertical axis. The colors used primarily include shades of green, red, yellow, brown, and cream.
title: Pa. German Pie Plate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
